blocking.section: Decision outcome (Kafka row); Decision outcome > Confirmation
blocking.issue: This is a regression from the L1-4 fix. The Kafka row now holds each record's `maxBufferedBytes` reservation until franz-go resolves its produce promise, even after the request has failed, but nothing bounds how long that takes. No record-delivery timeout is set, and the record is not tied to the request context. `maxBufferedBytes` is one budget per Node, shared with every HTTP gate and stream. During a Kafka outage, records whose publishes already returned 502 keep their reservations until franz-go gives up, if it ever does, while new publishes keep adding records until `MaxBufferedRecords` is reached. Every unrelated Route on the Node then gets 503 `RZ-RT-004`. One broker outage takes down the whole Node, and the Confirmation test cannot catch this: it checks only that reserved bytes stay within `maxBufferedBytes`, which the reservation rule makes true by construction.
blocking.evidence: Kafka row: "`MaxBufferedRecords` bounds the producer buffer ([source](https://github.com/twmb/franz-go/blob/master/docs/producing-and-consuming.md)), and each record keeps its `maxBufferedBytes` reservation until franz-go resolves its produce promise, even after the request has failed, so the Node budget bounds producer memory". Confirmation: "With the Kafka container paused, publishes end in 503 or 502 while the Node's reserved bytes stay within `maxBufferedBytes`". Configuration model, Body buffering and limits: "Across requests, all of it is reserved from `maxBufferedBytes`, one budget per Node: a gate that cannot reserve gets the 503 above".
blocking.fix: Append to the Kafka row: "each record is produced with its request context and a delivery timeout no longer than the Upstream `timeout` (setting unresearched; OQ-multi-protocol-8 spike), so an unsent record fails when its request ends and a sent one resolves within a bounded time". Add a Bad consequence: "Bad, because until the OQ-multi-protocol-8 spike confirms that bound, records held during a broker outage keep Node-wide `maxBufferedBytes` reservations after their requests fail, which can refuse unrelated Routes with 503 `RZ-RT-004`." Extend the paused-Kafka Confirmation sentence: "... and an `http` Route on the same Node keeps answering 200, and reservations return to zero within the Upstream `timeout` after the last publish".

blocking.issue: This is also a regression from the revision. The MQTT client row now tells autopaho to use an in-memory `Queue`, but it gives the queue no bound and does not say whether publishes pass through it. If they do, then while the external broker is down every publish is queued in memory. That memory is not reserved from `maxBufferedBytes`, and it is not released when the request times out with 502. Queued messages are then sent after the client has already seen a failure. This is the MQTT twin of the Kafka producer-buffer finding that L1-4 resolved: Node memory can grow without bound during a broker outage. The research names only the `Queue` field and gives no bound for it.
blocking.evidence: MQTT client row: "each Node connects with its own client identifier derived from `node.id` and the Upstream name, `CleanStartOnInitialConnection` true, `SessionExpiryInterval` 0 and an in-memory `Queue`, so no session or queue state outlives the connection (P4, pack 8.11; ...)". Research: "autopaho `ClientConfig` fields include ... `CleanStartOnInitialConnection`, `SessionExpiryInterval` and `Queue`" (no bound documented). ADR driver: "the client MUST report acknowledgment and buffer limits".
blocking.fix: Add to the MQTT client row: "QoS 1 publishes go directly on the connection, never through the `Queue`, so a disconnected client fails the attempt at once (502 `RZ-UP`) and nothing is held after the request ends; if autopaho cannot publish without the queue (unresearched; OQ-multi-protocol-8 spike), each queued message keeps its `maxBufferedBytes` reservation until it is sent or dropped, and the queue is bounded". Extend the integration-test Confirmation: "with the Mosquitto container paused, `mqtt` publishes end in 502 within the Upstream `timeout` and the Node's reserved bytes return to zero".

non_blocking.section: Decision outcome (MQTT client row); More information
non_blocking.suggestion: The row marks the client-identifier and session rule as "proposed for Multi-protocol under OQ-multi-protocol-8", but More information lists only the depguard amendment. Add a second bullet: "Proposed amendment: [Multi-protocol](../architecture/07-multi-protocol.md#kafka-nats-jetstream-and-mqtt) SHOULD adopt the per-Node MQTT client identifier and non-persistent session rule (OQ-multi-protocol-8)". Then the owning document can pick it up.

The owning document calls the one-message `Consume()` pre-buffer "setting unresearched" and an OQ-multi-protocol-10 spike. Add "(setting unresearched; OQ-multi-protocol-10 spike)" to the NATS row so readers do not take it as a confirmed library capability.

The research mentions `MaxBufferedRecords` only together with `ManualFlushing` for batching. Say that the Node uses it without `ManualFlushing` to cap buffered records, or cite that capability as unresearched under the OQ-multi-protocol-8 spike.
